responsibilities.responsibility: Background-stream retention default, absent-setting and explicit-value persistence policy
responsibilities.old_owner: BackgroundStreamPreferences selected a BuildConfig-dependent absent default, BackgroundStreamService had two independent five-minute recovery fallbacks, and ConsoleActivity wrote the preference key directly
state_moved: explicit retention value persistence including zero/off and no-limit
effects_moved: SharedPreferences write for an explicit selection
service restart and missing-extra fallback resolution through the same preference owner
callers_migrated: Game lifecycle/park/warm-up callers were already routed through BackgroundStreamPreferences and remain so
obsolete_paths_removed: BackgroundStreamService hardcoded five-minute field and command fallbacks
responsibilities.production_wiring_evidence: BackgroundStreamPreferencesTest executes the production owner against absent and explicit stores and inspects every direct Game/Service/Console production path. S02-RETENTION-DEBUG/RELEASE/MIGRATION and S02-HOME-PICKER-SEPARATION all pass.
responsibilities.packaging_evidence: S02-ANDROID-PACKAGE-WIRING finds BackgroundStreamPreferences and BackgroundStreamService in the debug APK and release R8 mapping, and verifies release classes.dex after both builds pass.
responsibilities.lifetime_notes: The preference is Android-local durable configuration. No eager migration write occurs: an absent key resolves to 30 minutes, while any explicit stored integer remains authoritative. RetainedStreamSessionCoordinator continues to own in-process Home/picker retention without a timeout; S07 physical transport ownership is unchanged.

remaining_monolith_responsibilities: Game still owns the physical NvConnection/decoder/input/audio lifecycle assigned to S07; S02 does not claim Activity-destruction survival.
ConsoleActivity keeps presentation state for the selected settings label, but no longer owns persistence or default/migration semantics.
test_seam: Package-visible SharedPreferences overloads let unit tests exercise the exact read/write policy used by the public Context entrypoints without adding Robolectric or a new abstraction.
